equation_request.abstract: The quantum Fourier transform (QFT) is a key ingredient of several quantum algorithms and a qudit-specific implementation of the QFT is hence an important step toward the realization of qudit-based quantum computers. This work develops a circuit decomposition of the QFT for hybrid qudits based on generalized Hadamard and generalized controlled-phase gates, which can be implemented using selective rotations in NMR. We experimentally implement the hybrid qudit QFT on an NMR quantum emulator, which uses four qubits to emulate a single qutrit coupled to two qubits.

specification.problem: Construct the quantum Fourier transform on a hybrid qudit register (mixed dimensions) via a decomposition into generalized Hadamard and generalized controlled-phase gates. The abstract mentions an NMR emulation of one qutrit plus two qubits but gives no explicit equations.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful instance: hybrid register of one qutrit (d=3) and two qubits (d=2), total dimension 12, with standard QFT definition and a standard mixed-radix Hadamard/controlled-phase decomposition. Out of scope: the paper's specific gate decomposition, the NMR selective-rotation pulse sequences, the four-qubit qutrit emulation encoding, and experimental results and fidelities.

symbols.meaning: total Hilbert space dimension, product of d_j
primitive N-th root of unity exp(2 pi i/N)
generalized controlled-phase gate between qudits with dimensions d_a and d_b
symbols.domain: diagonal unitary on C^{d_a} tensor C^{d_b}

equations.label: QFT definition
equations.description: QFT on the full hybrid register of dimension N, where the register basis is identified with integers 0..N-1.
equations.justification: Standard QFT definition; the abstract names the QFT but states no equation.

equations.label: Generalized Hadamard
equations.description: Single-qudit DFT used as the generalized Hadamard; d=3 for the qutrit, d=2 gives the ordinary Hadamard.
equations.justification: Common definition of generalized Hadamard; the paper's exact convention is not given in the abstract.
assumptions: Sign and normalization convention may differ from the paper

equations.label: Mixed-radix encoding
equations.description: Register ordering: qutrit most significant, then the two qubits.
equations.justification: Needed to make the QFT well defined on the hybrid register; ordering is a proposed choice.

equations.label: Generalized controlled-phase
equations.description: Diagonal two-qudit phase gate, with m the product of the relevant dimensions for the mixed-radix phase 2 pi k_a k_b / m (e.g. m dividing the cumulative radix).
equations.justification: Generic form of generalized controlled-phase; the actual phase schedule of the paper is not specified in the abstract.
assumptions: Phase denominators m must be derived from the mixed-radix factorization of eq_1; not derived here

equations.label: Decomposition form
equations.description: Schematic structure of a QFT decomposed into Hadamards and controlled-phases, followed by a digit-reordering permutation.
equations.abstract_quote: a circuit decomposition of the QFT for hybrid qudits based on generalized Hadamard and generalized controlled-phase gates
equations.justification: The abstract states the decomposition uses these gate types; the detailed ordering and phases are the usual qubit-QFT analogue and are not given.
assumptions: Exact gate ordering and phases not verified; digit-reversal permutation may be needed

specification.initial_state: Arbitrary computational basis state |x_0,x_1,x_2> (e.g. |0,0,0> or a chosen test state); not specified in the abstract.

steps.description: Encode input integer x in mixed-radix digits across the qutrit and two qubits.
Apply generalized Hadamard on the qutrit, then controlled-phase gates between qutrit and each qubit.
Apply Hadamard on the first qubit and a controlled-phase with the second qubit, then Hadamard on the last qubit.
Apply the digit reordering to match the QFT output convention; compare with the target transform.

assumptions: Chose the qutrit plus two qubits instance to match the abstract's emulated system.
Standard QFT and DFT conventions used as background.
Mixed-radix phase factors are not derived or verified here.
missing_information: Exact gate decomposition, phase angles, and gate ordering of the paper
Mapping of the qutrit onto two-qubit emulation levels
